comparison.objective: Sets a proximity-sensor gap with a feeler leaf and secures it with a cam clamp; the candidate sets a gripper opening stop and locks a threaded adjuster.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-2229 requires positioning a sensor against a third-body gauge and closing a lever; the candidate requires simultaneous coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque so a jam nut does not rotate the screw.
comparison.success_condition: PR-2229 checks a 1.00±0.25 mm gap, gauge removal/return, closed lever, and hands-off stability; the candidate checks a retained 90° opening after three released cycles, nut retention, drift, and clearance.
comparison.reason: Both set and retain an adjustment, but the candidate uniquely tests coupled screw–jam-nut counterholding and post-lock articulated cycling rather than gauge-mediated placement and cam clamping.

review_notes: New proximity sensor feeler-gap setting then cam-lock. Compare retention/third-body gauge/locking; angles versus millimeters or cycle count alone not distinction.
